R001.fact: A nonzero integer has nonzero image in C; each natural factorial has nonzero image in C, and finite products of nonzero complex scalars are nonzero. If c≠0 in C, scalar multiplication by c on a complex vector space is invertible.

grounds.reason: λ≥0 supplies the positive integer factors λ−t in the stated finite ranges.
V is a complex vector space and v≠0.
e_i is normalized by the complex image of i!.

R001.justification: The usual integer embedding into C is injective: its real part is the same integer. Factorials are finite products of positive integers, with 0!=1; fields have no zero divisors. Multiplication by c inverse inverts nonzero scalar multiplication. This justifies nonvanishing and cancellation in S001, S002, S004 and S005.

R001.fact: If (e_i) is a finite complex basis of V, every z∈V has a unique expansion z=Σ_i b_i e_i. If h e_i=μ_i e_i and hz=νz, then (μ_i−ν)b_i=0 for every i.

grounds.reason: F003 proves that the finite family e is a complex basis of V.
F001 provides h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i and its all-natural-power identity gives hz=(−λ−2)z.
z=y^(λ+1)v is a vector of V and b is chosen as its coordinate family.

R001.justification: Spanning gives the finite expansion, and independence gives uniqueness by subtracting two expansions. Linearity of h and subtraction of νz give Σ_i(μ_i−ν)b_i e_i=0. Independence forces each coefficient to vanish. This is the coefficient comparison already used in S004.

R001.fact: For λ∈Z with λ≥0 and n=λ.toNat+1, Fin n has cardinal n and its indices identify bijectively with natural i satisfying i≤λ.

grounds.reason: H001 gives λ≥0.
D001 defines n=λ.toNat+1.

R001.justification: Fin n consists of the natural numbers less than n, namely 0,…,n−1. Since n=λ.toNat+1, these are exactly the natural indices at most λ.toNat, giving the identification and cardinality needed in S003.

R002.fact: For the finite complex basis (e_k)_(0≤k≤n) asserted by N001, prescribed images w_k∈V determine a unique complex-linear endomorphism T with T(e_k)=w_k. Two complex-linear maps agreeing on all these basis vectors are equal. Thus the displayed E_ij exist uniquely, and the proof's evaluations on the basis determine the asserted endomorphism identities.

grounds.reason: N001 explicitly supplies the complex basis (e_k)_(0≤k≤λ).
λ≥0 identifies its indexing with the finite natural interval 0,…,n, n=λ.toNat.

R002.justification: Write each u∈V uniquely as Σ_(k=0)^n a_ke_k and set T(u)=Σ_(k=0)^n a_kw_k. Unique basis coordinates ensure the definition is well defined. Coordinate addition and scalar multiplication prove linearity. Any linear map with these images must have this formula, giving uniqueness and equality from basis evaluations.

R002.fact: For natural n and 0≤j≤n, binom(n,n−j)=binom(n,j), and binom(n,0)=binom(n,n)=1. For n=λ.toNat these give exactly the endpoint coefficients and c_j used in S001, also after the canonical casts into ℤ and ℂ.

grounds.reason: H001 supplies nonnegative λ, so λ is the integer cast of n=λ.toNat.
D005 defines c_j as the integer cast of Nat.choose(n,j).
S001 restricts i,j to the natural interval 0,…,λ and displays the symmetric factorial quotients.

R002.justification: For 0≤j≤n the binomial coefficient has factorial quotient n!/[j!(n−j)!]. Exchanging j and n−j leaves the denominator unchanged; its factorials are positive integers. At j=0 or j=n the quotient equals one. These finite combinatorial identities establish precisely the coefficients used here without any inversion of c_j.

R003.fact: Set n=λ.toNat. Under H001, the integer cast of n equals λ and n<p. For natural r with integer cast r≤λ, r≤n and r<p. In particular n itself is an allowed instance of F001 in S002; any natural j≤λ also satisfies j≤n.

grounds.reason: Gives 0≤λ
Uses arbitrary natural r≤λ.

R003.justification: A nonnegative integer is the integer cast of its natural representative. Natural-to-integer casting preserves and reflects order, so the stated index comparisons and r

R003.fact: For n=λ.toNat and j≤n, casting M005 into K gives (c_j in K)·(j! in K)·((n−j)! in K)=(n! in K). The image of D equals ∏_{t=0}^{n}(c_t in K).

grounds.reason: K is a field, so its canonical natural and integer casts exist.
Provides the natural factorial identity for j≤n.
Defines c_j as the integer cast of choose(n,j).
Defines D as the finite integer product of c_t.

R003.justification: The canonical casts preserve 1, addition and multiplication, and the natural cast agrees with composition through the integers. Applying these maps preserves the factorial identity, and induction on the finite number of factors preserves the defining product for D. Because j≤n, the notation λ−j in the prose represents the same nonnegative subtraction n−j.

R003.fact: In K every unit is nonzero, and a finite product of nonzero elements is nonzero. A product containing a zero factor is zero. These facts apply respectively to the units in S001, the coefficient identity in S002, and the finite product defining D.

grounds.reason: K is a field, with 1≠0 and inverses for nonzero elements.
M004 establishes the factorial units in S001.
The factorial identity and F001 establish coefficient nonvanishing before the product argument.
D has finitely many indexed factors.

R003.justification: A unit equal to zero would give 1=0 upon multiplication by its inverse. If a,b≠0 and ab=0, multiplying by a inverse gives b=0, a contradiction. Induction starting with the empty product 1 proves the finite-product assertion. The zero-factor assertion follows from multiplication by zero and associativity. These supply the routine field reasoning already used in the two paragraphs.

R004.fact: Every element of M⊗_Z K or K⊗_Z M is a finite sum of pure tensors. Thus additive maps from either tensor product agreeing on all pure tensors agree everywhere. In S002 this extends the displayed scalar-compatibility identity for σ to all U, proving σ is K-linear; its additive inverse equivalence is K-linear too. It also justifies identifying the conjugated operator with D009's induced operator and checking transferred operator equalities on pure tensors.

grounds.reason: U is the balanced tensor product of the integer modules M and K, with the specified K-action.
The induced operator is specified by its additive pure-tensor formula once preservation is established.
K is a field, hence has its usual additive integer-module structure.
M is an additive subgroup with its integer-module structure.
M007 supplies the additive flip equivalence and its pure-tensor formula.
F001 establishes preservation and integer linearity for every operator being extended.
S002 checks scalar compatibility and the conjugate's action explicitly on pure tensors.

R004.justification: The balanced tensor product is the quotient of the free abelian group on pairs by the additivity and balancing relations. Pure-tensor classes generate it additively; negatives can be absorbed in either factor. Equalities between additive maps therefore extend from these generators to finite sums. For fixed b∈K, the additive maps u↦σ(bu) and u↦bσ(u) agree on pure tensors by S002, so they agree everywhere. Bijectivity then gives σ^{-1}(bw)=bσ^{-1}(w). The same generator argument proves equality of the additive induced operators and extends the displayed operation identities.

R005.fact: If V is a finite-dimensional complex vector space of dimension n and an integer basis of M has images forming a complex basis of V, then this common basis has a finite index set of cardinal n and can be reindexed by Fin n, preserving both basis properties.

grounds.reason: H002 gives the finite complex dimension λ+1.
H003 supplies an integer basis whose images form a complex basis.
H001 gives λ≥0, so D001 identifies the natural n with λ+1.
D001 defines n as λ.toNat+1.

R005.justification: Take a complex basis with n elements, as furnished by finite dimension. The finite exchange argument bounds any finite independent family by the size of a finite spanning family: successively insert independent vectors into the spanning list and remove a vector with a nonzero coefficient, retaining spanning and the vectors previously inserted. Thus the supplied basis cannot have n+1 distinct indices and its index set is finite. If its size is k, applying the same bound in both directions to the two bases gives k≤n and n≤k, hence k=n. A bijection Fin n to its index set reindexes both the integer and complex families; bijections preserve finite relations and spanning expansions.

R005.fact: Every element of either balanced integer tensor product M⊗_Z K or K⊗_Z M is a finite sum of pure tensors. For the K-actions used here, the additive flip σ(m⊗a)=a⊗m is therefore K-linear, and its inverse is K-linear.

grounds.reason: D008 specifies U=M⊗_Z K and d·(m⊗a)=m⊗da.
H003 supplies the integer module M.
H001 supplies the field K and its integer-module structure.
M002 supplies the scalar-extended K-module and its basis on K⊗_Z M.
M007 supplies the additive flip equivalence and its pure-tensor formula.

R005.justification: The balanced tensor product is the additive group generated by pure tensors subject to the additive and balancing relations; negative generators can be absorbed into a tensor factor. Consequently each element is a finite sum of pure tensors. On such a tensor σ(d·(m⊗a))=(da)⊗m=d·σ(m⊗a), and additivity and distribution extend this equality to finite sums. For w in the target, σ(d·σ⁻¹(w))=dw=σ(σ⁻¹(dw)); injectivity gives d·σ⁻¹(w)=σ⁻¹(dw). Thus the inverse is also K-linear.

R006.fact: For U=M⊗_Z K, if S,T are complex-linear maps preserving M, their induced K-linear maps satisfy (ST)^K=S^K T^K. Thus the induced four-factor product defining A_ij equals the corresponding product of induced divided powers. Equality of K-linear maps on all pure tensors m⊗a implies equality on U.

grounds.reason: D008 defines U as the balanced tensor product with the indicated K-action.
D009 gives the pure-tensor action of the induced maps.
N007 supplies M-preservation and Z-linearity of every divided-power restriction.
D006 identifies the underlying four-factor operator A_ij.
N004 supplies A_ij^K as the induced operator of the restriction.

R006.justification: Composition preserves M and Z-linearity. On m⊗a, both (ST)^K and S^K T^K give S(T(m))⊗a. The balanced tensor product is generated additively by pure tensors: it is the quotient of the free abelian group on pairs by the bilinear and balancing relations. Hence agreement on these generators implies equality of linear maps. Iterating the two-factor identity proves the four-factor identity; N007 guarantees all intermediate vectors lie in M.

R007.fact: For m=λ.toNat and n=m+1, the natural indices 0≤i≤m correspond bijectively to Fin n by their values. Transporting N004's family along this bijection preserves its conditional multiplication formula and its diagonal sum identity.

grounds.reason: Defines n=λ.toNat+1.
λ≥0 identifies λ with the integer represented by λ.toNat.
Supplies the operator family, its products and its diagonal sum.

R007.justification: For a natural index i, i≤m is equivalent to i<m+1. The correspondence is therefore bijective and preserves equality of indices. Substitution into N004's multiplication formula gives the transported conditional product. The diagonal summands are each enumerated exactly once, so the finite sum remains Id_U.

R008.fact: For a complex-linear endomorphism T of V and an additive subgroup M of V with T(M) contained in M, the restriction T|_M is an endomorphism of the induced integer module M. This applies to x,y,h and every X_r,Y_r here.

grounds.reason: V is a complex vector space; x,y,h are complex-linear endomorphisms; M is an additive subgroup with its induced integer-module structure.
Each X_r is a complex scalar multiple of a power of the complex-linear x, hence is complex-linear.
Each Y_r is a complex scalar multiple of a power of the complex-linear y, hence is complex-linear.
F001 establishes preservation of M by x,y and every X_r,Y_r.
Before the restriction step, S002 establishes preservation of M by h using H002 and subgroup closure.

R008.justification: Complex linearity gives additivity. Additivity implies T(0)=0 and T(-m)=-T(m); repeated addition gives T(nm)=nT(m) for natural n, and the negative case gives the identity for all integers. Preservation makes these identities identities in M, proving integer-linearity of the restriction.

source_steps.text: By H001, λ is nonnegative, so natural bounds use λ.toNat=λ and n=λ+1. For every natural i, induction gives h y^i v=(λ−2i)y^i v: at i=0 this is hv=λv; if it holds at i, then hy^(i+1)v=(yh−2y)y^iv=(λ−2i−2)y^(i+1)v. Independently, x y^i v=i(λ−i+1)y^(i−1)v for i≥1. At i=1, xyv=yxv+hv=λv. Assuming this formula at i≥1, the preceding h formula gives xy^(i+1)v=(yx+h)y^iv=[i(λ−i+1)+λ−2i]y^iv=(i+1)(λ−i)y^iv. Both induction assumptions are discharged in their steps. Iterating the x formula for 0≤i≤λ gives x^iy^iv=i!·∏_(t=0)^(i−1)(λ−t)v. Every factor is a positive integer in C for i≥1 in this range; for i=0 the scalar is one. Since v≠0, y^iv and e_i are nonzero. Dividing the first formula by i! gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

To test independence, fix arbitrary a and temporarily assume L1: Σ_(i=0)^λ a_i e_i=0. For arbitrary j in the range apply ∏_(k=0,k≠j)^λ(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). The h-eigenvector formula F001 makes all summands except j vanish. The remaining equation is a_j ∏_(k≠j)2(k−j)e_j=0. Every 2(k−j) is nonzero in C because k≠j, and e_j≠0 by F001; hence a_j=0. This also covers λ=0, when the operator product is the identity. Discharge L1: a zero linear combination has all coefficients zero. Since a and j were arbitrary, the indexed family (e_i)_(0≤i≤λ) is complex linearly independent.

Apply M001 with scalar field C, ambient space V, finite index type {0,…,λ}=Fin n, and vector family e restricted to that index set. H002 supplies dim_C V=λ+1 and finite dimension; H001 gives n=λ+1, so the number of indices is its dimension. F002 supplies independence. M001 yields span_C{e_i:0≤i≤λ}=V, hence these independent vectors form a basis.

Set z=y^(λ+1)v and expand z=Σ_(i=0)^λ b_i e_i using F003. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Subtracting this from the h-action on the expansion and using independence gives 2(λ+1−i)b_i=0 for each i≤λ. This scalar is nonzero in C, so every b_i=0 and z=0. All further y powers on v vanish. From F001 and the definitions, xe_0=0 and xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; directly from factorials ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, while z=0 gives ye_λ=0. Together with the h formula these are all asserted generator actions.

For every 0≤i≤λ and r≥0, repeated use of F004 gives x^r e_i=[(λ−i+r)!/(λ−i)!]e_(i−r) if r≤i, and zero if r>i because x kills e_0. Similarly y^r e_i=[(i+r)!/i!]e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ, and zero past the top endpoint because y kills e_λ. These products follow by induction on r, starting with the empty product and multiplying the next coefficient at each step. Divide by r! in C, which is nonzero. Apply M005 first to its natural parameters (λ−i+r,r) when r≤i and second to (i+r,r) when i+r≤λ; the second parameter is at most the first in both cases. The identity choose(N,r)r!(N−r)!=N! identifies the respective scalar ratios as binom(λ−i+r,r) and binom(i+r,r). Thus the X_r,Y_r formulas hold with exactly the zero cases stated in the output statement. F003 and F004 supply its other clauses.

Use the basis in N001 to define E and set Q=Y_λX_λ. The divided-power formulas give X_λe_k=0 for k<λ and X_λe_λ=e_0, while Y_λe_0=e_λ. Hence Q=E_(λλ). For every i≤λ, X_(λ−i)e_λ=e_i since its coefficient is binom(λ−λ+(λ−i),λ−i)=1; therefore X_(λ−i)Q=E_(iλ). For every j≤λ, QY_(λ−j) kills inputs e_k with k<j because they land below λ, kills inputs with k>j by termination, and sends e_j to binom(λ,λ−j)e_λ=c_j e_λ. Here binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j), as seen from the identical factorial ratios λ!/[j!(λ−j)!]. Thus QY_(λ−j)=c_jE_(λj).

By D006 and F001, for all i,j in the index set A_ij=X_(λ−i)QY_(λ−j)=c_j E_ij. By H003 every divided power factor in this expression belongs to U_Z and preserves M, and a composition of maps preserving M preserves M. Thus each A_ij preserves M; this uses no assertion that E_ij itself preserves M.

Evaluation on the basis gives E_ijE_kl=δ_(jk)E_il and Σ_i E_ii=Id_V. Using F002, A_ijA_kl=c_jc_lδ_(jk)E_il=δ_(jk)c_j A_il. Also Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii=Σ_i(∏_t c_t)E_ii=D Id_V. These use only integer coefficients. Empty products equal one, so the calculation also covers λ=0. Together with F002 these prove every clause of the output statement.

For every natural r≤λ, H001 gives r<p. Apply M004 with ring K, its characteristic p from H001, and source natural n=r. The right side of its equivalence holds, so r! cast into K is a unit and hence nonzero in the field K. This includes r=0, whose factorial is one.

For every natural j≤λ, apply M005 with source n=λ.toNat and k=j. Cast its identity c_j j!(λ−j)!=λ! into K. Since λ! is nonzero by F001, the left side is nonzero; if c_j had zero image its product would be zero. Thus every c_j has nonzero image. A finite product of nonzero elements of a field is nonzero, by induction on the number of factors and the absence of zero divisors. D is precisely that product, so its image is nonzero. This proves the output statement with the factorial statement F001.

H003 gives stability under every X_r,Y_r. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M; N002 gives stability under every A_ij. Each is complex linear, so its restriction to the additive subgroup M is integer linear. Every identity involving these operators, their compositions and integer scalar multiples restricts to M by pointwise equality in V. In particular the N002 multiplication and diagonal identities restrict, and the defining divided-power identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r restrict for all natural r. No action on a tensor product is used before this preservation is established.

Instantiate M003 over Z→K with the integer module M and the endomorphisms in F001. Obtain ρ. Instantiate M007 with tensor factors M,K to obtain σ. Although M007 only asserts additivity, σ is K-linear for the actions in use: for every pure tensor m⊗a and scalar b∈K, σ(b·(m⊗a))=σ(m⊗ba)=ba⊗m=b·σ(m⊗a). Extend this equality by additivity since pure tensors span, and likewise for its inverse. For any integer endomorphism t of M, conjugating ρ(t) by σ gives on m⊗a precisely t(m)⊗a. Thus this conjugate is exactly the D009 induced map whenever t is a restriction in F001. On pure tensors, ρ respects addition, composition and identity; for instance ρ(s)ρ(t)(a⊗m)=a⊗s(t(m)) and ρ(Id)(a⊗m)=a⊗m. Equality holds on all tensors by their finite-sum presentations. Integer scalar multiples also extend to the same integer cast in K by balancing, including negative integers by additivity. Conjugation preserves these identities. Consequently T↦T^K for the lattice maps in F001 preserves their sums, products, identity, integer scalars and powers.

By N003 all c_j and D have nonzero images in K; their inverses therefore exist. Define F as stated. Transfer the N002 identities by F002. For all 0≤i,j,k,l≤λ, F_ijF_kl=c_j^(-1)c_l^(-1)δ_(jk)c_j A_il^K=δ_(jk)c_l^(-1)A_il^K=δ_(jk)F_il. The transferred diagonal identity is D Id_U=Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii^K, with coefficients now cast to K. Since D=c_i∏_(t≠i)c_t and c_i,D are nonzero, D^(-1)∏_(t≠i)c_t=c_i^(-1). Multiplying the transferred identity by D^(-1) gives Σ_i F_ii=Id_U. These conclusions are valid when λ=0 as well.

Finally apply F002 to the two divided-power identities in F001. For every 0≤r≤λ this gives (r! in K)X_r^K=(x^K)^r and (r! in K)Y_r^K=(y^K)^r. No division by a factorial is used in transferring them. These identities and F003 are the complete output statement.

H001 identifies λ with its natural value and gives n=λ+1>0. Let ι=Fin n. By H003 an integer basis of M is also a complex basis of V. H002 says V has finite complex dimension λ+1=n. Therefore the index set of that supplied basis is finite with exactly n elements, and it can be relabelled by ι. This is the defining basis-cardinality characterization of finite dimension: any complex basis of an n-dimensional complex space has n elements. Thus there exists an integer basis of M indexed by ι which is a complex basis of V.

Choose such a basis b using F001 and H003. Its integer span is all of M and its integer coordinates are unique. The identity of this choice is private to this proof; only its scalar extension and cardinality will be used.

Apply M002 to the base ring Z, canonical Z-algebra K and the integer basis b from F002, obtaining the K-basis B of K⊗_Z M with B_i=1⊗b_i. Apply M007 to obtain σ. It is K-linear: for all m∈M,a,d∈K, σ(d·(m⊗a))=da⊗m=d·σ(m⊗a), and pure tensors span. The same calculation applies to the inverse. Thus σ is a K-linear equivalence for the K-action in D008.

Define bK_i=σ^(-1)(B_i)=b_i⊗1. F003 implies this is a K-basis of U: apply σ to finite linear relations for independence, and pull back expansions in B for spanning. Apply M006 to field K, vector space U, index type ι and basis bK. It gives dim_K U=Nat.card ι=n=λ+1. This finite basis also proves finite dimensionality. Since n>0 by F001, the index 0 exists and its basis vector bK_0 is nonzero, so U≠0. This proves both clauses of the output statement; the conclusion is independent of the chosen b.

N007 establishes that x,y,h and every X_r,Y_r preserve M and have integer-linear restrictions, so every one of their induced operators in D009 is defined. N004 supplies A_ij^K and the family F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1)A_ij^K. N003 supplies the nonzero coefficients in this formula. By H001 the indices 0≤i,j≤λ have λ−i,λ−j,λ all within 0,…,λ.

Fix W and introduce L1: W is invariant under x^K,y^K,h^K. Invariance under x^K and y^K implies invariance under every power of these operators, by induction on the exponent with identity as base and composition as step. For each 0≤r≤λ, N003 gives r!≠0 in K, and N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)(x^K)^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)(y^K)^r. A K-subspace is closed under scalar multiples, so it is invariant under all these X_r^K,Y_r^K.

For every i,j in the range, D006 and the induced tensor formula imply A_ij^K=X_(λ−i)^K Y_λ^K X_λ^K Y_(λ−j)^K. Indeed the right side applied to a pure tensor m⊗a is (X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j)m)⊗a, the defining action of the left side; N007 guarantees every intermediate lattice vector stays in M, and pure tensors span U. F001 and F002 therefore show W is invariant under A_ij^K. Scalar closure then shows W invariant under F_ij=c_j^(-1)A_ij^K. The h-invariance premise has no further use.

Discharge L1. For the arbitrary K-subspace W, invariance under the induced x,y,h therefore implies invariance under all the displayed F_ij. Universal introduction in W proves the output statement exactly, with all induced maps already constructed in S001.

H001 and D001 give n=λ+1≥1, so the integers 0,…,λ correspond bijectively to Fin n. Reindex the N004 family by this bijection, obtaining F. N004 gives F_ijF_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0) and Σ_i F_ii=Id_U; equality of indices and finite sums are preserved by this bijection. N005 gives dim_K U=λ+1=n and U≠0, and hence finite dimensionality. N007 gives integer restrictions of x,y,h, so the induced actions mentioned in the conclusion are defined and are exactly D009's operators on U.

Fix an arbitrary K-subspace W and introduce L1: W is invariant under the induced x,y,h. Apply N006 to W. Its operators are the same F as here because N006 and N004 give the identical expression (c_j in K)^(-1)(X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j))^K; reindexing does not change the maps. Therefore W is invariant under every F_ij. Apply E001 with its field=K, space=U, natural parameter=n, operator family=F and subspace=W. H001 gives the field, F001 gives finite dimension n and both matrix-unit identities, and the preceding application of N006 gives invariance. E001 yields W=0 or W=U.

Discharge L1 and universally quantify W: every K-subspace invariant under the induced x,y,h is zero or U. Combine with the nonzero assertion in F001 and U=M⊗_Z K=V(K). H001 allowed every field of characteristic p and every 0≤λ<p. No step requires algebraic closure or distinct weights in K. When λ=0 the index set has one element; when p=2 the permitted λ are 0,1 and the same argument applies. This is exactly P, with the original induced action.

For every natural r, X_r and Y_r belong to the subalgebra U_Z by its definition as the integer algebra generated by all these operators. H003 says M is stable under this algebra, so X_r(M)⊆M and Y_r(M)⊆M. In particular, since 1!=1, X_1=x and Y_1=y; thus x,y preserve M.

H002 identifies the given endomorphism h with xy−yx. For every m∈M, F001 places x(y(m)) and y(x(m)) in M; since M is an additive subgroup, their difference is in M. Therefore h(M)⊆M. Every listed complex-linear map is additive and respects integer multiples; its restriction to M is consequently an integer-linear endomorphism. This proves the output statement without using any induced operator or assuming any further hypothesis.

header:
import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
open Module
universe u v
namespace SL2Lattice
variable {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
noncomputable def dp (t : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (Nat.factorial r : ℂ)⁻¹ • t ^ r
noncomputable def vec (y : Module.End ℂ V) (w : V) (i : ℕ) : V := dp y i w
def n (l : ℤ) : ℕ := l.toNat + 1
def coeff (l : ℤ) (j : ℕ) : ℤ := (Nat.choose l.toNat j : ℤ)
def detCoeff (l : ℤ) : ℤ := ∏ j : Fin (n l), coeff l j.val
def otherCoeff (l : ℤ) (i : Fin (n l)) : ℤ :=
  ∏ j ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (n l))).erase i, coeff l j.val
noncomputable def raw (l : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (i j : Fin (n l)) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  dp x (l.toNat - i.val) * dp y l.toNat * dp x l.toNat * dp y (l.toNat - j.val)
def Stable (M : Submodule ℤ V) (t : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : V, m ∈ M → t m ∈ M
def Inv {R : Type v} [Field R] {U : Type u} [AddCommGroup U] [Module R U]
    (W : Submodule R U) (t : Module.End R U) : Prop :=
  ∀ w : U, w ∈ W → t w ∈ W
structure Actions (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) where
  xZ : Module.End ℤ M
  yZ : Module.End ℤ M
  hZ : Module.End ℤ M
  XZ : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  YZ : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  x_eq : ∀ m : M, (xZ m : V) = x (m : V)
  y_eq : ∀ m : M, (yZ m : V) = y (m : V)
  h_eq : ∀ m : M, (hZ m : V) = h (m : V)
  X_eq : ∀ r (m : M), (XZ r m : V) = dp x r (m : V)
  Y_eq : ∀ r (m : M), (YZ r m : V) = dp y r (m : V)
def rawZ {M : Submodule ℤ V} {x y h : Module.End ℂ V}
    (a : Actions M x y h) (l : ℤ) (i j : Fin (n l)) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  a.XZ (l.toNat - i.val) * a.YZ l.toNat * a.XZ l.toNat * a.YZ (l.toNat - j.val)
noncomputable def red (K : Type v) [Field K] {M : Submodule ℤ V}
    (t : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) :=
  t.baseChange K
noncomputable def matrixUnit (K : Type v) [Field K] {M : Submodule ℤ V}
    {x y h : Module.End ℂ V} (a : Actions M x y h) (l : ℤ)
    (i j : Fin (n l)) : Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) :=
  (coeff l j.val : K)⁻¹ • red K (rawZ a l i j)
end SL2Lattice
open SL2Lattice

P.explanation: The public parameters range over every prime p, arbitrary field K with CharP K p, integer 0≤l<p, complex highest-weight module V, nonzero highest vector w and arbitrary admissible M. H002 expresses the given sl₂ representation through its three generators with the exact commutators, finite dimension l+1 and invariant-subspace irreducibility; these are equivalent to the source module data because the generators form a basis of sl₂(ℂ). M as a ℤ-submodule is the same additive subgroup. H003's simultaneous Fin q bases are obtained by reindexing the source basis, which is finite since it is a complex basis of finite-dimensional V; conversely they are exactly an integer basis also complex, and generator stability is equivalent to stability under Uℤ. No relation between this basis and the divided-power basis is imposed. T011 checks the additive tensor flip M⊗ℤ K→K⊗ℤ M, scalar compatibility with multiplication on K and intertwining of every restricted integer operator. Thus it is a K-linear identification for the source action, in both directions; subspaces, nonzeroness and invariant-subspace dichotomies correspond under it. Actions packets are restrictions agreeing after the injective inclusion M→V, unique pointwise, and T017 supplies their existence from H002/H003. Existence plus the universal dichotomy over all packets is therefore equivalent to the dichotomy for the original induced x,y,h, and Nontrivial is precisely V(K)≠0. The finrank n argument uses l≥0; no algebraic closure, distinct reduced weights, p≠2 or l>0 is assumed.

conclusion.statement: The vector space V(K)=M⊗_Z K is nonzero, and every K-linear subspace invariant under the induced x,y,h is either zero or all of V(K), for all the original parameters including λ=0, p=2, and arbitrary fields K of characteristic p.

Nontrivial (TensorProduct ℤ K M) ∧ Nonempty (Actions M x y h) ∧ (∀ a : Actions M x y h, ∀ W : Submodule K (TensorProduct ℤ K M),

representation: V and K range over arbitrary universes u and v; K is only a field. λ remains an integer l, n=l.toNat+1, and Fin n indexes precisely 0,…,λ under H001. M is the equivalent integer submodule of its additive subgroup, with no topological/discreteness condition. Endomorphism multiplication is composition, rightmost first; powers and inverse factorial scalar multiples define X,Y without asserting lattice preservation. H002 retains commutators, highest vector, dimension and irreducibility via generator-invariant subspaces. H003 retains an arbitrary simultaneous integer/complex basis, reindexed by Fin q since the complex dimension is finite; stability under the generated integer algebra is equivalent to stability under all its divided-power generators by sums, products, integer scalars and identity. We compute in K⊗ℤ M so Mathlib's K-module structure acts on the first factor; T011 checks the tensor flip, original right-factor scalar action and all induced operators. Actions is only the data of integer restrictions with equality after inclusion, not an added hypothesis: T017 proves its existence. All downstream statements quantify over every such packet; injectivity of M→V makes the operators unique. F is definitionally the normalized reduction of the four-factor rawZ product. Nontrivial is the assertion that the vector space is nonzero. Basis and E witnesses stay with their identifying equations. No localization or residue-field representation is introduced.

namespace YuiBasis
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B001 : ∀ (K U : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup U] [Module K U] [FiniteDimensional K U] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] (v : ι → U), LinearIndependent K v → Fintype.card ι = Module.finrank K U → Submodule.span K (Set.range v) = ⊤ := by
  intro K U _ _ _ _ ι _ v hv hc
  exact hv.span_eq_top_of_card_eq_finrank' hc
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B002 : ∀ (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] (ι : Type*) (b : Basis ι ℤ M), ∃ B : Basis ι K (TensorProduct ℤ K M), ∀ i : ι, B i = TensorProduct.tmul ℤ (1 : K) (b i) := by
  intro K M _ _ _ ι b
  refine ⟨b.baseChange K, ?_⟩
  intro i
  exact b.baseChange_apply K i
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B003 : ∀ (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M], ∃ ρ : Module.End ℤ M →+* Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M), ∀ (t : Module.End ℤ M) (a : K) (m : M), ρ t (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a m) = TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a (t m) := by
  intro K M _ _ _
  let ρ : Module.End ℤ M →+* Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) :=
    { toFun := fun t => t.baseChange K
      map_one' := by exact LinearMap.baseChange_one ℤ M
      map_mul' := by intro f g; exact LinearMap.baseChange_mul f g
      map_zero' := by exact LinearMap.baseChange_zero
      map_add' := by intro f g; exact LinearMap.baseChange_add f g }
  refine ⟨ρ, ?_⟩
  intro t a m
  rfl
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B004 : ∀ (A : Type*) [Ring A] (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP A p] (n : ℕ), IsUnit (Nat.factorial n : A) ↔ n < p := by
  intro A _ p _ _ n
  exact IsUnit.natCast_factorial_iff_of_charP (A := A) p
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B006 : ∀ (K U : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup U] [Module K U] (ι : Type*) (b : Basis ι K U), Module.finrank K U = Nat.card ι := by
  intro K U _ _ _ ι b
  exact Module.finrank_eq_nat_card_basis b
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B007 : ∀ (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M], ∃ e : TensorProduct ℤ M K ≃+ TensorProduct ℤ K M, ∀ (m : M) (a : K), e (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ m a) = TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a m := by
  intro K M _ _ _
  letI : Module ℤ (TensorProduct ℤ M K) := TensorProduct.instModule
  letI : Module ℤ (TensorProduct ℤ K M) := TensorProduct.instModule
  refine ⟨(TensorProduct.comm ℤ M K).toAddEquiv, ?_⟩
  intro m a
  rfl
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B008 : ∀ (K U : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup U] [Module K U] [FiniteDimensional K U] (n : ℕ) (F : Fin n → Fin n → Module.End K U), Module.finrank K U = n → (∀ i j k l, F i j * F k l = if j = k then F i l else 0) → (∑ i : Fin n, F i i) = 1 → ∀ W : Submodule K U, (∀ i j (w : U), w ∈ W → F i j w ∈ W) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤ := by
  classical
  intro K U _ _ _ _ n F hdim hmul hsum W hW
  by_cases hbot : W = ⊥
  · exact Or.inl hbot
  right
  obtain ⟨w, hw, hw0⟩ := Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot hbot
  have hex : ∃ j : Fin n, F j j w ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra hn
    have hz : ∀ j : Fin n, F j j w = 0 := by simpa using hn
    have hs := congrArg (fun f : Module.End K U => f w) hsum
    have : w = 0 := by simpa [LinearMap.sum_apply, hz] using hs.symm
    exact hw0 this
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hex
  let u : U := F j j w
  have hu0 : u ≠ 0 := hj
  have huW : u ∈ W := hW j j w hw
  have huu : F j j u = u := by
    have ht := congrArg (fun f : Module.End K U => f w) (hmul j j j j)
    simpa [Module.End.mul_apply, u] using ht
  let v : Fin n → U := fun i => F i j u
  have hact (k i : Fin n) : F j k (v i) = if k = i then u else 0 := by
    have ht := congrArg (fun f : Module.End K U => f u) (hmul j k i j)
    change F j k (F i j u) = _
    by_cases hki : k = i
    · simpa [Module.End.mul_apply, hki, huu] using ht
    · simpa [Module.End.mul_apply, hki] using ht
  have hli : LinearIndependent K v := by
    apply Fintype.linearIndependent_iff.mpr
    intro g hg k
    have ht := congrArg (fun x : U => F j k x) hg
    have hs : g k • u = 0 := by
      simpa [map_sum, map_smul, hact] using ht
    exact (smul_eq_zero.mp hs).resolve_right hu0
  have hspan : Submodule.span K (Set.range v) = ⊤ :=
    YuiBasis.B001 K U (Fin n) v hli (by simpa using hdim.symm)
  apply top_unique
  rw [← hspan]
  apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
  rintro x ⟨i, rfl⟩
  exact hW i j u huW

end YuiBasis
